summary: Router 0.19.0 makes concrete model names an explicit grant (ADR-0052, supersedes ADR-0046, closes SK-SEC-05 / TM-04). auth.client_allows now allows a concrete name only for the router's own UI client or when the client's models value is the boolean true; before, a missing value meant true. config._parse_client_auth rejects a non-boolean models value, stores false when it is missing and logs a warning naming the client unless it has inference: false. The admin client listing reports models as the boolean grant. Traced callers: both concrete-name decisions in proxy.py (lines 146 and 1054) go through client_allows with concrete = not a role, so Ollama, OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic paths share the check; unauthenticated requests in observe mode stay unrestricted as before (mode enforce + locked in the reference deployment, TM-01). UI-saved client fields still coerce models to bool (admin._client_spec), and UI-created clients without the field now get roles only. Model listings still show concrete names (information, not access). The memory, session and context self-tests call concrete models and now carry the explicit grant, which is the documented migration. Breaking for deployments relying on the old default; the changelog and warning name the fix. Rebased onto main after #93 (router 0.18.3, agent 0.28.0, ADR-0051 for agent configuration keys): this change now carries ADR-0052 and router 0.19.0; the v0.26.0 changelog row joins both; tests re-run on the rebased tree.

findings.evidence: router 0.18.2 auth.client_allows: `if c.get("models", True): return None` let a role-limited client without a models setting call any concrete model.
findings.resolution: Fixed: explicit boolean grant required (auth.py, config.py); selftest_security covers missing, true, non-boolean, UI client and configuration default; the new checks fail against the old code.

tests.evidence: All PASS, including 'missing models setting denies concrete names', 'models:true keeps concrete names', 'only the boolean true grants concrete names', 'the router's own UI client keeps concrete names', 'config: missing models becomes false', 'config: a non-boolean models value is rejected'.

tests.command: Negative check: python test/selftest_security.py with router/skirnir_router/auth.py and config.py from origin/main (git stash)
tests.evidence: rc=1, AssertionError: missing models setting denies concrete names; the new test detects the old default.

tests.command: Every `python test/...` and `python router/...` command of the router CI job (ci.yml), except integration/e2e
tests.evidence: No failures, including selftest_context, selftest_memory, selftest_interoperability, selftest_sessions, selftest_rerank, selftest_config_load; router.py --check config.example.yaml --pure: configuration ok.
All checks passed; ADR index ok: 52 ADRs.

limitations: PostgreSQL session-store integration and the nightly end-to-end suite were not run locally; CI runs the PostgreSQL job.
Deployments must add models: true where concrete names are needed before upgrading; the reference deployment already sets models explicitly for every client.
Per-client model allowlists and filtering concrete names out of listings for role-only clients are left open.
